title: Jaw-Jaw With Belarus, Revisited Amid Ukraine War
gist: Michael Kimmage, revisiting his 2021 call for realistic US diplomacy with Belarus, argues Belarus remains an exceptionally dangerous Russia–West flashpoint. War has been avoided only because Lukashenko is still in power while letting Russia's military entrench, and the risk of conflict after his eventual exit is higher now than in 2021. (Members-only article, partial text.)

insights.claim: Belarus remains an exceptionally dangerous potential flashpoint between Russia and the West even though it served as a staging ground for Russia's invasion of Ukraine without triggering direct confrontation with NATO.
insights.speaker: Michael Kimmage
insights.so_what: Belarus is a persistent tail-risk node for European security; NATO's eastern flank risk premium should not fade simply because no clash has occurred.
insights.quote: Belarus remains an exceptionally dangerous potential flashpoint between Russia and the West.
insights.locator: Belarus remains an exceptionally dangerous potential

insights.claim: Conflict over Belarus has been avoided since 2021 because Alexander Lukashenko has stayed in power, keeping some distance from the Ukraine war while letting Putin do as he wishes on Belarusian territory, where the Russian military is dug in and ubiquitous.
insights.speaker: Michael Kimmage
insights.so_what: Stability hinges on one aging ruler; leader-succession is the key variable to monitor for Belarus-related escalation.
insights.quote: he has also allowed Russian President Vladimir Putin to do what he wishes on Belarusian territory, where the Russian military is dug in and ubiquitous
insights.locator: Belarus remains an exceptionally dangerous potential

insights.claim: The risk of military tensions or outright war following Lukashenko's eventual departure is greater today than it was in 2021.
insights.speaker: Michael Kimmage
insights.so_what: A Lukashenko succession event would be a discrete geopolitical shock for Eastern Europe — watch his health and succession signals.
insights.quote: the risk that military tensions or even outright war might follow Lukashenko’s departure from the scene, when that occurs, is greater today than it was in 2021
insights.locator: Belarus remains an exceptionally dangerous potential

insights.claim: Lukashenko and Putin would be content if they can find a political leader to uphold the existing regime in Belarus, and European countries would not challenge a Belarus under tacit Russian control since that is already the status quo.
insights.speaker: Michael Kimmage
insights.so_what: A managed regime-continuity succession is the benign scenario; Europe is not a source of escalation in that case.

insights.claim: Lukashenko's domestic legitimacy has long been eroding: he has no discernible vision and has alienated Belarus from all neighbors other than Russia, and Kimmage draws a parallel to Ukraine in 2014.
insights.speaker: Michael Kimmage
insights.so_what: Eroding legitimacy raises the odds of a 2014-Ukraine-style popular upheaval during succession — the destabilizing scenario that could draw in Russia and the West.
insights.quote: He has no discernible vision for his country, which he has unnaturally alienated from all of its neighbors other than Russia.

insights.claim: In 2021 Kimmage argued the United States should adopt a realistic diplomatic relationship with Belarus that accounts for its strategic partnership with Russia and learns from overpromises made to Ukraine.
insights.speaker: Michael Kimmage
insights.so_what: Signals a realist school in US policy favoring engagement with Minsk over promises of Western integration — relevant to any US-Belarus thaw.

insights.claim: US policy toward Belarus should avoid repeating overpromises the West made to Ukraine, given Belarus's entrenched strategic partnership with Russia.
insights.speaker: Michael Kimmage
insights.so_what: Implies limited Western appetite to back a Belarusian opposition, reducing odds of a contested Western-aligned transition.
insights.quote: learns from overpromises made to Ukraine
